coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Palindrome numbers from 1 to N
coding.question: Given a number N, print all the palindrome numbers from 1 to N (both included) in increasing order. A palindrome number reads the same from left to right and from right to left, for example 7, 44 and 121.
coding.output_format: One line: the palindrome numbers from 1 to N separated by single spaces.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
# TODO: write your logic here
print(n)
coding.solution:
n = int(input())
res = [str(x) for x in range(1, n + 1) if str(x) == str(x)[::-1]]
print(" ".join(res))
hints: Reverse the digits of each number and compare with the original.
In Python, str(x)[::-1] gives the reversed string.
coding.explanation: Check every number from 1 to N: reverse its digits and compare. Each check takes O(d) for d digits, so the total is O(N log N) and fast for N up to 10^5.
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Bubble sort
coding.question: Sort an array of N integers in increasing order using bubble sort. Bubble sort repeatedly walks through the array and swaps two neighbours when the left one is bigger than the right one. Print the sorted array, and on the next line the total number of swaps bubble sort made.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N integers separated by spaces.
coding.output_format:
Line 1: the sorted array, values separated by single spaces.
Line 2: the total number of swaps.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
swaps = 0
# TODO: write your logic here
print(" ".join(map(str, a)))
print(swaps)
coding.solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
swaps = 0
for i in range(n):
    done = True
    for j in range(n - 1 - i):
        if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
            a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
            swaps += 1
            done = False
    if done:
        break
print(" ".join(map(str, a)))
print(swaps)
hints: After pass i, the i largest values are already at the end.
Count a swap only when two neighbours are actually exchanged.
coding.explanation: Bubble sort makes passes over the array, swapping neighbours that are out of order; if a pass makes no swap the array is sorted and we stop early. The number of swaps equals the number of inversions. Time O(N^2), which is fine for N up to 1000.
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.title: Maximum pair sum with equal digit sums
coding.question: Given an array of n positive integers, find two different elements (different positions) whose digit sums are equal and whose total is as large as possible. Print that largest total, or -1 if no two elements have the same digit sum. Example: 51 has digit sum 6 and 42 has digit sum 6, so they can be paired.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n integers.
coding.output_format: One integer: the largest pair total, or -1.
coding.starter_code:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
# TODO: group numbers by their digit sum
print(-1)
coding.solution:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
best_by_sum = {}          # digit sum -> largest number seen with that digit sum
ans = -1
for x in a:
    ds = sum(int(c) for c in str(x))
    if ds in best_by_sum:
        ans = max(ans, best_by_sum[ds] + x)
        best_by_sum[ds] = max(best_by_sum[ds], x)
    else:
        best_by_sum[ds] = x
print(ans)
hints: Numbers can only pair with numbers of the same digit sum.
For each digit sum, remember only the largest number seen so far.
coding.explanation: Walk the array once; for each number compute its digit sum and pair it with the largest earlier number having the same digit sum (stored in a dictionary). O(n * digits) time.
coding.label: AI practice

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Merge overlapping intervals
coding.question: You are given n time slots as intervals [start, end]. Merge all intervals that overlap or touch (for example [1, 3] and [3, 5] become [1, 5]) and print the merged intervals in increasing order of start.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: two integers start and end.
coding.output_format: One line per merged interval: start and end separated by a space.
coding.starter_code:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0])
iv = [(int(d[1 + 2 * i]), int(d[2 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n)]
# TODO: sort by start, then merge
for s, e in iv:
    print(s, e)
coding.solution:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0])
iv = sorted((int(d[1 + 2 * i]), int(d[2 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n))
merged = [list(iv[0])]
for s, e in iv[1:]:
    if s <= merged[-1][1]:                 # overlaps or touches
        merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], e)
    else:
        merged.append([s, e])
print("\n".join("%d %d" % (s, e) for s, e in merged))
hints: Sort the intervals by start time first.
Then an interval either extends the last merged one (start <= last end) or begins a new one.
coding.explanation: After sorting by start, scan once: if the next start is at most the current end, extend the end; otherwise close the current interval and start a new one. O(n log n) for the sort.

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Minimum jumps to reach the end
coding.question: You are standing at index 0 of an array of n non-negative integers. arr[i] is the maximum jump length from index i (you can jump any number of steps from 1 to arr[i]). Find the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index. If the last index cannot be reached, print -1. If n is 1 you are already there, so print 0.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n integers.
coding.output_format: One integer: the minimum number of jumps, or -1.
coding.starter_code:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
# TODO: greedy (BFS by levels) or DP
print(-1)
coding.solution:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
jumps, cur_end, farthest = 0, 0, 0
ans = 0
if n > 1:
    ans = -1
    for i in range(n - 1):
        if i > farthest:            # cannot even stand here
            break
        farthest = max(farthest, i + a[i])
        if i == cur_end:            # must jump now
            jumps += 1
            cur_end = farthest
            if cur_end >= n - 1:
                ans = jumps
                break
print(ans)
hints: Think of it as levels: all indexes reachable with 1 jump, then with 2 jumps, and so on.
Track the farthest index reachable; when you reach the end of the current level, you must take one more jump.
coding.explanation: Greedy BFS by levels: cur_end is the farthest index reachable with the current number of jumps, farthest is the best reach from inside this level. When i hits cur_end, take a jump and extend to farthest. If i ever passes farthest, the end is unreachable. O(n) time.
coding.label: AI practice
coding.source_note: Written for practice on Capgemini's reported coding topics

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Count subarrays with sum K
coding.question: Given an array of N integers (values can be negative) and an integer K, count how many subarrays (continuous parts of the array) have a sum exactly equal to K.
coding.input_format:
Line 1: two integers N and K.
Line 2: N integers separated by spaces.
coding.output_format: One integer: the number of subarrays whose sum is K.
coding.starter_code:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(0)
coding.solution:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
seen = {0: 1}
s = count = 0
for x in a:
    s += x
    count += seen.get(s - k, 0)
    seen[s] = seen.get(s, 0) + 1
print(count)
hints: A subarray (i, j] has sum K when prefix[j] - prefix[i] = K.
Store how many times each prefix sum has appeared in a dictionary.
coding.explanation: Walk the array keeping the running prefix sum s. Every earlier prefix equal to s - K starts a subarray ending here with sum K, so add its count from a hash map. Time O(n), space O(n). A two-pointer window does not work here because values can be negative.
